# pbs_node_acme (Resource)

Manages the ACME settings of a Proxmox Backup Server node: which ACME account (`pbs_acme_account`) orders the certificate of its web interface and API, and for which domains, each validated by a challenge plugin (`pbs_acme_plugin`). `pbs_node_certificate` orders the certificate; PBS renews it with these settings.

The node is a singleton: creating the resource takes over the node's ACME settings, replacing domains configured before, and destroying it removes them. It manages only these settings — `acme` and `acmedomain0` to `acmedomain4` in the node's configuration — and leaves the node's other settings alone.

Reading the settings needs `Sys.Audit on /system`, changing them `Sys.Modify on /system`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The node orders its certificate with the account of the pbs_acme_account
# example, for two names validated through Cloudflare, by the plugin of the
# pbs_acme_plugin example — both assumed in the same configuration.
resource "pbs_node_acme" "this" {
  account = pbs_acme_account.letsencrypt.name

  domains = [
    { domain = "pbs.example.net", plugin = pbs_acme_plugin.cloudflare.id },
    { domain = "backup.example.net", plugin = pbs_acme_plugin.cloudflare.id },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `account` (String) Name of the ACME account that orders the node's certificate, such as the `name` of a `pbs_acme_account`. PBS checks it when it orders.
- `domains` (Attributes Set) Domains of the certificate, 1 to 5, each in a slot of its own in PBS (`acmedomain0` to `acmedomain4`). The certificate covers all of them; the CA picks which one becomes its subject — Let's Encrypt the alphabetically first. A domain keeps its slot while it stays, so reordering them changes nothing. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--domains))

### Optional

- `node` (String) Node whose ACME settings to manage: `localhost`, which every PBS answers to, or the node's host name. Defaults to the provider's `node`. PBS is a single node, so both name the same settings: manage them with one resource only. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same value as `node`, present because Terraform requires an `id`.

<a id="nestedatt--domains"></a>
### Nested Schema for `domains`

Required:

- `domain` (String) Domain to certify, such as `pbs.example.org`. Each domain may appear once, in any case. PBS does not support wildcard domains.

Optional:

- `alias` (String) Domain whose `_acme-challenge` TXT record a DNS plugin sets instead of the domain's own, for a domain whose `_acme-challenge` record is a CNAME delegating the challenge to another zone: with an alias of `validation.example.net`, the CNAME points at `_acme-challenge.validation.example.net`.
- `plugin` (String) ID of the plugin that validates the domain, such as the `id` of a `pbs_acme_plugin`. Without one, the built-in `standalone` plugin validates it by HTTP on port 80, which the CA must reach.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_node_acme.this
  identity = {
    node = "localhost"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `node` (String) Node name, such as `localhost`.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_node_acme.this
  id = "localhost"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The ACME settings of a node are imported by the node's name: localhost, or
# its host name.
terraform import pbs_node_acme.this localhost
```
